prompt: A manufacturing company produces a product with the following initial cost structure: Raw materials cost $15 per unit. Labor cost is 40% of the raw materials cost. Overhead is 25% of the combined raw materials and labor cost. The company sets its selling price to achieve a 20% profit margin *on the selling price*. Due to recent market changes, the raw material cost increases by 10%, while labor cost *decreases* by 5% (from its original amount). Overhead remains fixed at 25% of the *new* combined raw materials and labor cost. The company decides to adjust its selling price to absorb 40% of the *total increase in production cost* and pass the remaining 60% of that increase onto the customer. What is the new selling price of one unit, rounded to two decimal places?
